## 9a287cf72db6

**Reproduced teaching-domain defect.** Generator SHA-256 `8b30ddfcadb4600b33cc452d541e7a28cdbb1d1404f63309529f566ae4292082`; selected rule hash `706561707b3a`.

`self_check` accepts the 7×14 input in `checks/audit/9a287cf72db6/input.json` with three solid 4×4 prototype panels and transform codes 1, 2, and 3. All three transforms are observationally invisible on these rotation/reflection-invariant panels. The selected Racket authority therefore produces exactly the same output as the executable identity-only decoder in `checks/audit/9a287cf72db6/identity_rival.json`. This means transform-code diversity alone does not guarantee the lesson identifies the transform stage.

Evidence: `checks/audit/9a287cf72db6/validator.json`, `finding.json`, `racket.json`, and `identity_rival.json`. Reproduction from `packet_root`: `python3 review.py run python3 -m arcpuzzles apply 9a287cf72db6 --input ../checks/audit/9a287cf72db6/input.json --out ../checks/audit/9a287cf72db6/racket-replay.json`. Suggested local fix: require at least one program-selected prototype/code pair whose transformed panel differs from identity, ideally for each non-identity transform used in the program.
